title: A 'forbidden' header builds a document the engine accepts, and the consumer that omits the header matches.
why: behavioural spec 'request': a 'forbidden' helper in a header map becomes the member's shape directly, not the 'each-like' the name-to-list rule would otherwise build. This is the end of the round trip, and the case that would have caught the defect: the wrapped document is refused by the engine with a pointer into an 'each-like' the author never wrote (shape spec §5.1), so an SDK that still wraps fails here rather than in a reviewer's reading. One variant, because 'forbidden' admits one point and contributes no dimension.

interaction.description: an order request that must not carry the customer's tax file number
